title: Helicopter travel throughout Vietnam
description: Larry's work as a radio operator took him up in helicopters a great deal, and he recalls travelling throughout Vietnam. The run he describes most exactly is the one to the mountain: "We took off from Ton Suhn Nhut to Nui Ba Den. We take off low for 10-15 miles and then we go up about 3000 to 5000 feet. The distance was about 70 miles. This would be in Rosethorn 007." Once, he and PFC Jones "got shot down and had to go back to the base and land." He names Lieutenant Hanna as a young pilot he flew with a couple of times, and thinks one of the aerial photographs may show the coast near Nha Trang.
researchNotes: 2026-09-14: the description no longer names a unit. It had said "what he remembers as the 118th AOD (Aviation Operations Detachment)", the founding brief's wording, which his son traced on 2026-09-13 to his own mishearing of an early conversation (data/recollections/2026-brief-118th-aod.json, provenance); the unit's name and number are open questions to be asked cold (ledger #2). "Substantial helicopter travel … throughout Vietnam" is the brief's paraphrase (2026-brief-helicopter-travel); the quotations are his transcribed words at VN-0071 and VN-0046 (2026-09-05) and the Nha Trang coast is VN-0090. The Tân Sơn Nhứt to Núi Bà Đen leg is about 85 km (53 statute miles) in a straight line; his 'about 70 miles' is close for a route flown many times, and the low-then-climb profile is standard for leaving a controlled airfield. The shoot-down with Jones has no date (ledger #34, issue #130). What he told of Hanna's later life is on his recollection and the person record, not here (ledger #31). Major Lewis stays in relatedPeople: on 2026-09-12 Larry withdrew Lewis as the face in VN-0016, not the flying he remembers with him (data/people/major-lewis.json); the interview guide asks that Lewis not be mentioned back to him. endDate follows the departure entry.
